name: crawlmark-mcp

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: List clients from clients.yaml. When Google is set up, Search Console sites and GA4 properties the account can access are discovered first and any new domains are added to clients.yaml (existing entries are never changed). Shows each client's domain, name, sources, properties, alternates and missing pieces, its SEO data provider (dataProvider, marked "(default)" when inherited) and Ahrefs/Semrush market (country), plus discovery status. Discovery is cached for a day; pass refresh to re-list. Clients without Google still work for DataForSEO, Lighthouse and axe.

refresh.description: Bypass the one-day discovery cache and list properties from Google again.

tools.name: monthly_report
tools.description: Build the data for a client's monthly SEO report. `vsPreviousMonth` and `vsLastYear` include a `previous` object, and `change` is null when the earlier period has no impressions. Covers: GSC clicks/impressions/CTR/position vs previous month and last year, GA4 organic sessions and key events, top and moving queries and pages (each query row carries `branded: boolean`), a branded vs non-branded split of clicks, impressions, CTR and impression-weighted position for the month and the previous one (query-level, so anonymized queries are excluded), top organic landing pages, and tracked keyword positions, plus an `audit` section: the latest saved audit and its diff against the most recent audit from before the month (`null` unless there is one from before the month and a newer one; a back-dated month still diffs against the latest audit). Also includes an `opportunities` section: the top 5 non-branded striking-distance queries, low-CTR top results and cannibalized queries for the month. Free by default (Google APIs only); set liveRanks for a paid live SERP check per tracked keyword (the whole run's estimate is checked against the budget first; when it does not fit, no check is made and `trackedKeywords.liveRanks` says why). Returns structured JSON for you to write up; each section reports its own error if a source is unavailable.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

month.description: YYYY-MM. Defaults to the last complete month.

liveRanks.description: Check live Google rank for each tracked keyword via DataForSEO (paid).

tools.name: list_report_templates
tools.description: Report templates available for a client: the builtin ones (`monthly`, `quarterly`, `executive` for a one-page summary, `technical` for web teams, `local` for local businesses), the global file (<home>/config/report-templates.yaml) and the client's own file (<home>/config/report-templates/<domain>.yaml), with each template's period, section count, optional sections (rendered only when asked for with `include`) and paid sections. Also reports whether each file exists and is valid; an invalid file never hides the builtin templates. Free and local.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

tools.name: get_report_template
tools.description: One report template with its defaults filled in (period, comparisons, sections) and the resolved branding (client file over global, field by field; the logo as a path plus whether it exists). Also returns `catalogue`: every section type with its title, group, cost (free, free with the user's own key, paid, or paid only with an option), what it needs and what it shows, for drafting templates with create_report_template. Free and local.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

template.description: Template id, e.g. monthly. See list_report_templates.

tools.name: validate_report_template
tools.description: Check report template YAML before saving it, or check the saved global or client file. Returns `valid`, `errors` with YAML paths (e.g. templates.monthly.sections[3].limit) and `warnings` (e.g. a logo file that doesn't exist). Give exactly one of `yaml` or `file`. No network, writes nothing.

file.description: Check the saved global file, or the client's file (needs client).

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

tools.name: create_report_template
tools.description: Draft a new report template from the user's request and save it to the global template file or a client's file, only after the user confirms. Pick sections from get_report_template's `catalogue` (free and paid types, what each needs). Never add a paid section unless the user asked for it; when they did, say what it costs per run (the proposal's paidSections estimates). Two steps, always: (1) call without confirmToken: nothing is saved; you get the template's YAML, a diff of the file, paid sections with estimates and a confirmToken (15 minutes, single use). Show the user the YAML and diff and ask. (2) Only after the user says yes, call again with exactly the same arguments plus confirmToken (and paidAcknowledged: true if it has paid sections the user explicitly agreed to). Saving fails if the file changed since the proposal. Clients that support it also ask the user directly before saving. Writes only report template files (never branding, clients.yaml or settings); comments in the file are kept and the previous version is saved as <file>.bak. Free and local.

client.description: Client domain or clients.yaml slug: needed for file: "client", and gives per-client cost estimates for paid sections.

file.description: Where to save: the global templates file (default) or the client's own file.

id.description: Template id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. board).

confirmToken.description: Only after the user said yes to the proposal you showed them: the token from the proposal call, with exactly the same other arguments.

paidAcknowledged.description: With confirmToken, when the proposal has paid sections: true only if the user explicitly agreed to those paid sections (by name and cost) in this conversation. Never set it on your own.

template.description: The template as JSON, validated with the template schema: { title, description?, period?: { range: last_month | last_quarter | last_n_days (days) | custom (start, end) }, compare?: [previous_period, previous_year], layout?: standard | onepage, sections: [{ id, type, optional?, paid?, title?, ...type options }] }. Section types and what they cost: get_report_template's `catalogue`. Paid section types need paid: true. Prefer optional: true for paid sections.

replace.description: Overwrite a template with this id in that file, or save your own copy of a builtin (monthly, quarterly, executive, technical, local) that then hides it.

Two steps, always: (1) call without confirmToken: nothing is saved; you get the template's YAML, a diff of the file, paid sections with estimates and a confirmToken (15 minutes, single use). Show the user the YAML and diff and ask. (2) Only after the user says yes, call again with exactly the same arguments plus confirmToken (and paidAcknowledged: true if it has paid sections the user explicitly agreed to). Saving fails if the file changed since the proposal. Clients that support it also ask the user directly before saving. Writes only report template files (never branding, clients.yaml or settings); comments in the file are kept and the previous version is saved as <file>.bak. Free and local.

tools.name: run_report_template
tools.description: Build a client's report from a template (default: the `monthly` template, the same data as monthly_report). Returns `reportId`, the period (with comparisons), each section's `status` (ok, error, unavailable, or skipped for a paid section without allowPaid) and `data`, computed `highlights` (facts only), `notes` and this run's paid `spend` (for you; report files never show it). Read each section's status before writing about it. The data is kept for 24 hours: pass `reportId` to export_report so the files show exactly these numbers. Free unless the template has a paid section and you set allowPaid: call it with estimateOnly: true first (no request, nothing spent), state the cost and what is left, and pass allowPaid only after the user agrees. Optional sections (e.g. cwv, gtm, issues, indexing) run only when listed in `include`.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

template.description: Template id (list_report_templates). Default: the template file's default, else monthly.

include.description: Optional section ids to include, e.g. ["cwv", "gtm"].

allowPaid.description: Run paid sections (only when the user asked; state the estimate first).

estimateOnly.description: Price the run's paid sections and return { estimateOnly, sections, total, remaining, wouldExceed, message } without fetching anything or spending. Use it before allowPaid.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Save a client report as Markdown, HTML, PDF and/or Word (docx) files under the reports folder (<home>/reports/<client>/<YYYY-MM>/<template>-<period>.<ext>; files 0600). Pass the `reportId` from run_report_template so the files show exactly the numbers you wrote about (kept 24 hours), or the same arguments as run_report_template to run it first. `narrative` is your commentary (summary plus text per section id; paragraphs, `- ` bullets and **bold** only; at most 30,000 characters); without it the files are labelled data-only. `inline: "html"` also returns a docs-friendly HTML copy (no logo, plain tables) for saving to Google Docs with the user's own Drive tool, only after the user agrees; `formats: []` with inline writes no file. Re-exporting the same template and period overwrites its files. Ask the user which format(s) they want (default PDF) and pass exactly those. PDF needs Chrome; if it fails, an HTML file is written instead (unless HTML was asked for too), the other formats are still written, and `warnings` says why.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

reportId.description: From run_report_template. Leave out the template and period arguments when you pass it.

estimateOnly.description: Price the paid sections without running anything or writing files (as run_report_template's estimateOnly). Not with reportId.

formats.description: Default: the saved default (the template file's defaults.formats), PDF unless changed. Pass exactly the formats the user chose.

narrative.description: Your commentary: `summary`, and text keyed by section id (e.g. search, brand, traffic, opportunities, audit).

inline.description: Also return the report as text (html is the Google Docs format).

tools.name: run_audit
tools.description: Audit a client's key pages: Lighthouse (performance, SEO, best practices, Core Web Vitals), axe-core WCAG checks, GSC index status per URL, GSC sitemap health, and a DataForSEO on-page check per URL. Optionally start a full-site crawl (paid, async; poll with crawl_status) and include a backlinks summary (paid). Takes ~30-60s per page because Lighthouse and axe run in a real browser; each browser check stops after 90s and the whole audit after 10 minutes. `urls` overrides go through the same URL checks as render_check (private addresses refused; RESTRICT_TO_CLIENT_DOMAINS applies).

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

urls.description: Override the client's keyPages for this run.

wcagLevel.description: WCAG conformance level for axe. Default AA.

backlinks.description: Include a backlinks summary from the client's data provider (DataForSEO, Ahrefs or Semrush; paid).

fresh.description: Default true: every check runs live, so the audit is a true snapshot (the on-page check is a paid call per page). false reuses cached results up to a day old.

cruxHistory.description: Also add real-user Core Web Vitals history (CrUX, free with CRUX_API_KEY or PSI_API_KEY) as site.cruxHistory, with findings for poor or needs-improvement LCP, INP and CLS in the latest period. Default false.

includeTagManager.description: Also audit the client's Tag Manager container (as gtm_audit does) as site.tagManager, with its findings (source gtm, medium or low; never alerts). Only when the user asks; default false.

localCrawl.description: Also run the free local crawl (as local_crawl does, up to 4 minutes inside the audit) as site.localCrawl, with its findings (source crawl); it is saved, so the orphan check can use it. Default false.

tools.name: technical_issues
tools.description: One deduplicated, severity-grouped list of a client's technical SEO problems from every stored source: the newest saved audit (Lighthouse, axe, URL Inspection, on-page and rendering checks), its site checks (robots.txt, sitemaps, orphans, AI crawlers), the newest local crawl, the newest stored DataForSEO full crawl within 30 days (its summary only; no crawl is started) and stored URL Inspection results. The same problem found by two sources is one item, listing both sources with their own severity; `affected` is the largest page count any one source reports. `changes` compares with the newest snapshot older than 24 hours: new, persistent, resolved (only when the source that reported it ran again) and unverified (not re-checked, never counted as fixed); null on the first run. Each call saves a snapshot (local). Never starts a crawl or audit; stale sources (older than maxAgeDays) are shown with their date. Free by default. The ahrefs_site_audit source reads the client's existing Ahrefs Site Audit project (clients.yaml ahrefsSiteAuditProject, else matched by domain) and spends units (50 for the issues, plus 50 per issueUrls call): it needs allowPaid: true and is read only (never starts a crawl or creates a project). Semrush's API has no Site Audit. Call with estimateOnly: true first, state the units and ask before passing allowPaid.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

sources.description: Default: every free source (audit, local_crawl, site_hygiene, dataforseo_crawl, gsc_inspection).

minSeverity.description: Leave out issues below this severity. Default low (everything).

issueUrls.description: Top issues to fetch up to 3 example URLs for from the Ahrefs Site Audit source (paid: one call each). Default 0.

maxAgeDays.description: Sources older than this are flagged stale. Default 45.

allowPaid.description: Needed for the Ahrefs Site Audit source (it spends Ahrefs units); set only after the user agreed to the estimate.

estimateOnly.description: Return the provider units this would spend, read nothing and save nothing.

tools.name: index_coverage
tools.description: Google's indexing of a client's site from stored URL Inspection results (the latest per URL): how many checked URLs are indexed, coverage states, the worst URLs (not found, soft 404, crawled or discovered but not indexed, duplicates, noindex, blocked by robots.txt), Google's canonical choices, Search Console sitemap errors and warnings, and the share indexed by month. It's a sample (key pages, top Search Console pages and a rotating sample of sitemap URLs), not Search Console's Page indexing report, which the API doesn't offer; fill it with inspect_index_coverage or crawlmark-cli index-coverage. `coverage` says how many of the sitemap URLs had a check in the last 30 days and whether that's all of them (complete) or a sample. Free and local apart from Search Console's sitemap list (cached a day). `quota` is today's URL Inspection use for the property (Pacific-time day).

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

tools.name: inspect_index_coverage
tools.description: Check how Google indexes a client's URLs with Search Console's URL Inspection API (free, read-only; it never asks Google to index anything) and store the results for index_coverage and the indexing_issues report section. Order: key pages not checked in `staleDays`, then the top 50 Search Console pages, then sitemap URLs never checked (a sample that rotates weekly), then the oldest checks. Stays within GSC_INSPECTION_DAILY_BUDGET per property per Pacific-time day (default 1,000 of Google's 2,000, so other tools keep headroom) and GSC_INSPECTION_PER_MINUTE (default 60); a quota error from Google stops the run and marks the day used up. `dryRun` counts what it would check per origin and inspects nothing. Takes about a second per URL. `all: true` checks every key page, top page and sitemap URL in the property not checked in `staleDays` when they fit in what's left of today's budget and this call's time (at most about 540 at 60 a minute, fewer when Google answers slower than one a second); otherwise it checks as many as fit and `fullPass` says how many daily runs a full pass needs (each run continues where the last stopped). `sitemapCoverage` says how many sitemap URLs have been checked in the last 30 days, and whether that's all of them.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

maxInspections.description: URLs to inspect in this run. Default 100. Leave out with all.

all.description: Check all pages (key, top Search Console and sitemap URLs) when today's budget allows; else continue the rotation and report how many runs a full pass needs.

staleDays.description: A URL checked more recently than this is skipped. Default 7.

dryRun.description: Plan only: counts per origin, no inspection.

tools.name: site_hygiene
tools.description: Site-level checks that need no browser: robots.txt (missing, blocks everything, blocks key pages, no Sitemap line), sitemaps (found via robots.txt and Search Console, indexes followed to depth 2 and 50 children; up to 50 URLs sampled for non-200, redirects and noindex; key pages missing from every sitemap), basic JSON-LD validation on key pages (required properties for Organization, LocalBusiness, Article, Product, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage; not the Rich Results Test), hreflang (self-reference, reciprocity, x-default), orphan pages (only when a complete crawl is already stored: the newest of a local_crawl (free) or a DataForSEO crawl, within 30 days; never starts a crawl), AI crawler access in robots.txt (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others: AI search vs training-only; a low finding only when an AI search crawler is blocked from the homepage or a key page) and llms.txt (informational: presence, llmstxt.org format, up to 10 same-host links checked; Google says it doesn't use llms.txt, so a missing file is not a finding). Every fetch is SSRF-guarded and size-capped. Uses raw HTML; run_audit uses the rendered DOM where it has a rendering result. Findings use source `site`; run_audit includes the same checks.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

fresh.description: Skip the one-day response cache. Default true.

tools.name: list_audits
tools.description: Saved run_audit snapshots for a client, newest first: audit ID, run time, page count, average scores and finding count. Use the IDs with get_audit and compare_audits. Free and local.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

tools.name: get_audit
tools.description: The full stored result of one audit, plus its normalised findings, by audit ID from run_audit or list_audits. Free and local.

tools.name: compare_audits
tools.description: Diff two saved audits of a client: new, resolved, persistent and unverified findings plus Lighthouse score changes. A finding counts as resolved only if its check ran successfully in the later audit; otherwise it is unverified. Defaults to the latest audit versus the one before it. Free and local.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

baseAuditId.description: The earlier audit. Default: the one before the target.

targetAuditId.description: The later audit. Default: the latest.

tools.name: crawl_status
tools.description: Check a full-site crawl started by run_audit. Returns progress, the on-page score, and a count of pages per issue (missing meta descriptions, duplicate titles, broken links, etc). Free to poll.

tools.name: crawl_issue_pages
tools.description: List the URLs from a finished crawl that fail one check, e.g. 'no_description', 'duplicate_title', 'is_broken', 'no_h1_tag', 'large_page_size'. Use the check names returned by crawl_status.

tools.name: spend_summary
tools.description: Paid API spend this calendar month, by client and provider, against the global cap. DataForSEO is billed in USD (cost_usd, totalUsd); Ahrefs and Semrush in their own API units (units per row, and `units.ahrefs` / `units.semrush` with this month's use and the global unit cap). Units are never converted to dollars. Spend recorded under a clients.yaml slug is counted under that client's domain.

tools.name: usage_summary
tools.description: How the tools have been used over the last N days (default 30): per tool, the number of calls, errors, error rate, error classes (e.g. TimeoutError, UrlRefusedError) and p50/p95 duration in ms. Only the tool, client, duration and outcome are logged, never other arguments. Free and local.

tools.description: Delete expired cache entries (fresh entries are kept) and tool-call usage rows older than 365 days.

Skips, with a reason, the client's own domain (and its subdomains), domains already listed, repeats and non-domains. Returns what was added, what was skipped and the full list. Free, local.

note.description: Optional note saved with each new entry, e.g. why it was added.

source.description: "manual" (default) when the user named them; "suggested" when they came from suggest_competitors and the user confirmed.

tools.description: A client's competitors from clients.yaml, with any note, source (manual or suggested) and date added, plus its area and niche. Free, local.

tools.description: Add tracked keywords to a client in clients.yaml (saved lowercase with single spaces). Skips, with a reason, keywords already tracked, repeats and empty ones. monthly_report reports their positions. Free, local.

note.description: Optional note saved with each new entry, e.g. why it was added.

tools.description: Remove tracked keywords from a client in clients.yaml (matched ignoring case and extra spaces). Free, local.

tools.description: A client's tracked keywords from clients.yaml, with any note, source and date added. Free, local.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

tools.name: set_client_profile
tools.description: Set a client's area, niche, display name or brand terms in clients.yaml. brandTerms are names people search for the brand (e.g. ["example plumbing", "ex plumbing"]); they add to the built-in domain and name matching used to split branded from non-branded queries, and the list you pass replaces the stored one ([] clears it). area is a DataForSEO location_name (City,Region,Country, e.g. "Austin,Texas,United States") used for local SERP searches; niche is a few words on what the client does (e.g. "emergency plumber"). dataProvider overrides the default SEO data provider for this client; it chooses whose paid data is used, not credentials. country is the ISO two-letter market Ahrefs and Semrush use (e.g. "US", "GB"). bingSite pins the Bing Webmaster Tools site bing_report reads (e.g. "https://www.example.com/"; it must be on the client's domain or a subdomain); unset, the domain is matched against your Bing key's verified sites. gbpPlaceId saves the client's Google Business Profile place ID (matched.placeId from local_profile) for local_profile, local_pack and local_reviews: set it only after the user has confirmed that local_profile found their business (it must be a place ID local_profile returned for this client in the last day). Pass an empty string to clear a field. Free, local.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

brandTerms.description: Replaces the client's brand terms; an empty array clears them.

dataProvider.description: Whose paid keyword, ranking, competitor and backlink data this client uses; "" clears the override (back to the default provider).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 market for Ahrefs/Semrush, stored uppercase (e.g. "US", "GB"); "" clears it.

bingSite.description: The Bing Webmaster Tools site URL for bing_report, as Bing lists it (e.g. "https://www.example.com/"); "" clears it (match by domain).

gbpPlaceId.description: The Google place ID local_profile returned (matched.placeId), saved only after the user confirms it is their business; "" clears it.

tools.name: suggest_competitors
tools.description: Suggest likely competitors for a client from two sources: organic keyword overlap from the client's data provider (DataForSEO, Ahrefs or Semrush), and live Google results from DataForSEO for up to 5 seed keywords (seeds you pass, the niche, tracked keywords, then top non-branded Search Console queries that relate to them) in the client's area (or its market when no area is set). Pass `seeds`: 3-5 non-branded service keywords (from the niche and homepage, confirmed with the user), since the client's own ranked keywords are mostly branded. Excludes the client's own site, current competitors, ignored domains and big platforms (social, directories, business-data sites, marketplaces, encyclopedias, .gov/.edu) and brand lookalikes (domains starting with the client's brand initialism or name). Returns ranked candidates with evidence, costUsd and fromCache. Paid (cached; costUsd for DataForSEO, `units` for Ahrefs/Semrush; without DataForSEO the SERP source is skipped with a note). Read-only: this never saves anything. Show the candidates and their evidence to the user, ask which to add, and only after they confirm call add_competitors with those domains and source: "suggested".

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

area.description: DataForSEO location_name for this search only, e.g. "Austin,Texas,United States". Defaults to the client's area.

niche.description: What the client does, for this search only. Defaults to the client's niche.

seeds.description: 3-5 non-branded service keywords to search first (e.g. 'modular home installation'). Never the client's brand name. For this search only.

tools.name: keyword_ideas
tools.description: Keyword ideas from seed keywords in the client's market: `related` (searches related to the seeds) or `matching` (keywords containing a seed). Each idea has volume, CPC, competition (0-1; null for Ahrefs), difficulty labelled by provider (dataforseo_kd, ahrefs_kd or semrush_kd: different 0-100 scales, never compare them), intent (DataForSEO only) and the seed. Paid through the client's data provider (DataForSEO in USD, Ahrefs or Semrush in API units), checked against the client's and the global monthly caps for the whole call before the first request. Call with estimateOnly: true first, tell the user the provider, the cost and what's left, and run it only after they agree; when the estimate doesn't fit, the message names a limit that does. Cached 7 days.

client.description: Client domain, e.g. 'example.com' (URL and www. forms also work), or a clients.yaml slug. Use list_clients to see options.

seeds.description: 1-20 seed keywords, e.g. the services the client sells (never just the brand name).

tools.name: suggest_brand_terms
tools.description: Infer how people search for a client by name, from that client's own queries: Search Console for the last 90 days (free). Only when the client has no Search Console property (or Google isn't set up) does it fall back to DataForSEO ranked keywords for its domain (paid, about $0.02, cached 7 days). If Search Console returns fewer than 20 rows it does not spend money unless you pass allowPaid: true (ask the user first); a Search Console error is reported, never retried on the paid source. Scores 1-3 word phrases its current brand matching misses on name similarity to the domain and name, navigational behaviour (top position with CTR far above the curve; Search Console only) and concentration across queries. Never proposes another client's brand (excluded with reason other-client-brand). Returns candidates with confidence (high/medium/low), score, evidence and source, the top non-branded queries no candidate covers, costUsd and fromCache. Each candidate has autoQualified and reviewReason: only candidates whose words match the distinctive part of the client's name (not trade words, places or company suffixes) are ever saved automatically. Read-only unless apply: true, which saves the auto-qualified candidates at or above minConfidence (default high) with source auto-gsc or auto-dataforseo. Then review every candidate with a reviewReason (e.g. needs-review: generic-name-match) and the remaining queries: show them to the user, and only for the ones they confirm call add_brand_terms with source: "suggested". Undo any term with remove_brand_terms.

client.description: Client domain (e.g. 'example.com'; URL and www. forms also work) or a clients.yaml slug. See list_clients.

tools.name: dataforseo_status
tools.description: Check the DataForSEO account: whether the credentials work, the mode (`sandbox` = canned free data, `live` = billed) from the configured base URL, and the account balance in USD. Free, never cached, records no spend, and never shows the credentials. A missing or rejected login is reported in the result, not as a tool error.

tools.name: ahrefs_status
tools.description: Check the Ahrefs API v3 key with Ahrefs' free limits-and-usage call: whether the key works, the plan, the key's and workspace's units used this billing month and when they reset, plus the units crawlmark recorded this calendar month against its own cap (monthlyUnitCap). Free (no API units), never cached, records no spend, and never shows the key. A missing or rejected key is reported in the result, not as a tool error. Change the key in a terminal (setup --step ahrefs), never through chat.

tools.name: semrush_status
tools.description: Whether a Semrush API key (v4, from the profile > API keys page) is set, what Semrush serves in crawlmark (keyword volume and backlinks; its v4 API has no rankings, competitors, visibility or Site Audit), and the units crawlmark recorded this calendar month against its own cap. Semrush has no free key check, so a rejected key shows on the first paid call. Free, never cached, records no spend, never shows a key. Change the key in a terminal (setup --step semrush), never through chat.

tools.name: lighthouse
tools.description: Run Lighthouse on any URL: category scores, lab Core Web Vitals and top opportunities. Adds real-user CrUX field data when PSI_API_KEY is set. Free, ~30s. http/https only; hosts that resolve to a private, loopback or link-local address are refused unless ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true, and with RESTRICT_TO_CLIENT_DOMAINS=true only client domains and their subdomains are allowed. Times out after 90s.

tools.name: accessibility_check
tools.description: Run axe-core WCAG checks on any URL. Returns violations grouped by rule with impact, WCAG criteria and example selectors. Automated checks catch a subset of issues; flag manual review in reports. Free. http/https only; hosts that resolve to a private, loopback or link-local address are refused unless ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true, and with RESTRICT_TO_CLIENT_DOMAINS=true only client domains and their subdomains are allowed. Times out after 90s.

tools.name: render_check
tools.description: Fetch a URL twice, as plain HTML (Googlebot-like user agent, no JavaScript) and as rendered by headless Chrome, then compare title, meta description, canonical, robots meta, H1s, links, JSON-LD types, hreflang, Open Graph and visible word count. Flags SEO elements that only appear after JavaScript runs (rules like title-js-only, canonical-mismatch, content-js-dependent). Free, ~15s, cached 1 day. http/https only; hosts that resolve to a private, loopback or link-local address are refused unless ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true, and with RESTRICT_TO_CLIENT_DOMAINS=true only client domains and their subdomains are allowed. Times out after 90s.

tools.name: setup_status
tools.description: Free. Reports, for each integration (config home, DataForSEO, the default data provider, Ahrefs, Semrush, Google, Search Console, GA4, Tag Manager, PageSpeed Insights key, Chrome, clients), whether it is `working`, `configured` (set but not verified), `missing` or in `error`, with a plain-language detail and the exact next step (a `crawlmark-cli` command for the user to run in a terminal, or a URL). Live checks are cheap (DataForSEO's free account check, a Google token check, cached property lists, one headless Chrome launch) and the whole result is cached for 60 seconds; `refresh: true` re-checks. Never returns secrets. Never ask the user to paste credentials into the chat: send them to the `next` command. Commands in `next` already use the result's `cli` field, which is how to run crawlmark-cli on this machine (it may be `node /path/dist/cli.js` or carry a CRAWLMARK_HOME prefix); use `cli` rather than a bare `crawlmark-cli` when writing any other command. Also reports the default SEO data provider (seoprovider row: which of DataForSEO, Ahrefs, Semrush is the default, where the setting comes from, and which are configured), repeated as the top-level `seoDataProvider` object, plus `ahrefs` and `semrush` rows. The provider is changed in a terminal with the command in its next field, never through chat.

refresh.description: Re-run the checks instead of using the 60-second cache.

instructions: SEO audit and reporting tools across Google Search Console, GA4, DataForSEO, Lighthouse and axe-core. Start with list_clients. If something isn't set up, call setup_status and give the user its next step; never ask them to paste credentials into the chat. Manage a client's competitors and tracked keywords with the add_/remove_/list_ tools; suggest_competitors proposes more (show them to the user and add only the ones they confirm). suggest_brand_terms infers the names people search a client by; confirm medium and low candidates with the user before add_brand_terms. For routine work use monthly_report and run_audit; use the lower-level tools for follow-up questions. Tools marked paid spend DataForSEO credit or Ahrefs/Semrush API units (whichever is the client's data provider) and are capped per client per month; prefer the free Google tools when they answer the question. Results are cached, so re-running a report is cheap.
